pages.quiz:
CREATIVE ARTS — TERMLY EXAM #12 (TERM 3)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. In a glide, your arms are (1 mark)
   A. stretched above the head with palms together
   B. folded
   C. behind your back
   D. by your sides

2. Which float has the body curled up like a ball? (1 mark)
   A. Mushroom float
   B. Prone float
   C. Glide
   D. Supine float

3. In a supine float, you lie (1 mark)
   A. standing
   B. face down
   C. on your back with ears in the water
   D. curled up

4. Why is it called the mushroom float? (1 mark)
   A. It tastes good
   B. It grows
   C. The back at the surface looks like the top of a mushroom
   D. It is very tall

5. A swimming cap is useful for (1 mark)
   A. drying
   B. making you float
   C. holding a whistle
   D. keeping long hair out of the way

6. In bubble blowing, you blow bubbles (1 mark)
   A. on land only
   B. slowly in the water
   C. with soap
   D. before you enter

7. After entering, you should (1 mark)
   A. move away from the edge so the next person can enter
   B. sit at the top
   C. pull others in
   D. stay at the edge

8. An elephant walk suits which rhythm? (1 mark)
   A. Very fast ta-te ta-te
   B. No beat
   C. Slow steady beats such as taa taa taa
   D. A whistle

9. A hare hop suits a rhythm that is (1 mark)
   A. absent
   B. very slow
   C. quick like ta-te ta-te
   D. silent

10. Who can teach you an indigenous game from your community? (1 mark)
   A. Only a computer
   B. Nobody
   C. An elder
   D. A stranger online

11. Learning about animals in games links to (1 mark)
   A. Space travel
   B. Agriculture
   C. Weather forecasts
   D. Swimming lessons only

12. Counting steps and jumps in animal games links to (1 mark)
   A. Mathematics
   B. Foreign languages only
   C. Geography maps
   D. Chemistry

13. Verse 3 of the anthem talks about (1 mark)
   A. the weather
   B. working together to build the nation and giving thanks
   C. cooking
   D. sports

14. The Kenya National Anthem is a (1 mark)
   A. a game
   B. a topical song about washing
   C. a work song
   D. national symbol

15. Why should you write the date on each work in your portfolio? (1 mark)
   A. To hide it
   B. To show when it was made
   C. For fun only
   D. To spoil it

16. What should be written on the portfolio label? (1 mark)
   A. A secret
   B. The price
   C. Nothing
   D. Your name, class and title

17. When someone comments on your work, you should (1 mark)
   A. listen quietly and say thank you
   B. argue
   C. walk away
   D. tear the work

18. How should you care for displayed works? (1 mark)
   A. Touch to feel the paint
   B. Do not touch or write on them
   C. Tear the corners
   D. Leave them in the rain

19. To appreciate a work of art means to (1 mark)
   A. hide it
   B. copy it exactly
   C. notice, understand and value it
   D. destroy it

20. A display portfolio holds (1 mark)
   A. only rubbish
   B. only rough drafts
   C. your best finished works
   D. tools

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Give four ways of caring for displayed works. (4 marks)

22. Why is it good to take different roles in animal games? (3 marks)

23. Explain what sportsmanship means and give two examples. (3 marks)

24. State four rules for playing the hawk and the chicks game. (4 marks)

25. Why do we play water games in shallow water with the teacher? (3 marks)

26. State three values taught by the Kenya National Anthem. (3 marks)

27. State the role of the Kenya National Anthem. (3 marks)

28. Why is swimming an essential life skill? (2 marks)

29. Describe how to do the crab walk and name the muscles it strengthens. (3 marks)

30. Name two animal movement games. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — TERMLY EXAM #12 (TERM 3) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — stretched above the head with palms together
   Arms overhead create a streamlined shape.

2. A — Mushroom float
   The tucked body with the back at the surface is the mushroom float.

3. C — on your back with ears in the water
   You look at the sky.

4. C — The back at the surface looks like the top of a mushroom
   The rounded back at the top looks like a mushroom cap.

5. D — keeping long hair out of the way
   Caps keep hair tidy.

6. B — slowly in the water
   You put your mouth in the water and blow out slowly.

7. A — move away from the edge so the next person can enter
   Make space for others.

8. C — Slow steady beats such as taa taa taa
   Slow heavy steps.

9. C — quick like ta-te ta-te
   Hares hop quickly.

10. C — An elder
   Elders know many traditional games.

11. B — Agriculture
   Agriculture teaches about animals.

12. A — Mathematics
   Counting is a maths skill.

13. B — working together to build the nation and giving thanks
   It calls for common effort and gratitude.

14. D — national symbol
   Like the flag, it stands for the nation.

15. B — To show when it was made
   Dates show how your skills grow.

16. D — Your name, class and title
   A label shows whose portfolio it is.

17. A — listen quietly and say thank you
   Good listeners grow.

18. B — Do not touch or write on them
   Care keeps them safe.

19. C — notice, understand and value it
   Appreciation is valuing with understanding.

20. C — your best finished works
   It is for showing to others.

SECTION B
----
21. (4 marks)
   Answer: Do not touch or write on them; keep away from water, sun and dust; keep neat labels; store in the portfolio flat afterwards. Any four.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: Everyone gets a fair turn, learns to lead and follow, and the team works better.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: Being fair and kind in sports. Examples: following the rules and shaking hands with the other team.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meaning, 1 mark for each example.

24. (4 marks)
   Answer: Hold but do not pull; the hawk tags gently; no pushing or tripping; stop at the whistle; take turns. Any four.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: To feel safe and in control, to learn to breathe and move with confidence and to avoid accidents.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: Unity, peace, justice, hard work, service, patriotism and thankfulness to God. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: It is a national symbol that unites Kenyans, shows love for the country and reminds us of our values.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

28. (2 marks)
   Answer: It helps people stay safe near water and prevent drowning, and it keeps the body fit.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

29. (3 marks)
   Answer: Sit, put hands behind, lift the hips and walk on hands and feet with tummy up. It strengthens the arms, shoulders and tummy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the position, 1 mark for walking, 1 mark for muscles.

30. (2 marks)
   Answer: Frog jump, crab walk, elephant walk, snake slither, hare hop, crocodile crawl, giraffe stretch, monkey swing. Any two.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.
